source: NCERT Class XII, Introductory Microeconomics, Ch. 2 (Theory of Consumer Behaviour).

sections.heading: 1. Utility and the Consumer
points: **Utility** = the satisfaction a consumer gets from consuming a good.
**Total Utility (TU)** = total satisfaction from all units; **Marginal Utility (MU)** = the addition from one more unit.
The consumer aims to **maximise satisfaction** with a limited **budget (income)** and given **prices**.

sections.heading: 2. Cardinal Utility Approach
points: **Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility** — as more of a good is consumed, the MU from each extra unit **falls**.
**Consumer's equilibrium (one good):** consume up to where **MU = price**.
**Two goods (Law of Equi-Marginal Utility):** allocate income so that **MU per rupee is equal across goods** (MUx/Px = MUy/Py).

sections.heading: 3. Ordinal Utility — Indifference Curves
points: **Indifference curve** = combinations of two goods giving the consumer **equal satisfaction**.
Properties: **downward sloping, convex to origin (diminishing MRS), never intersect; higher curve = more satisfaction**.
**Marginal Rate of Substitution (MRS)** = the rate at which a consumer trades one good for another (falls along the curve).
**Budget line** = combinations affordable with given income and prices.
**Consumer equilibrium:** where the budget line is **tangent** to the highest indifference curve (MRS = price ratio).

sections.heading: 4. Demand
points: **Law of Demand** — other things equal, as price **falls**, quantity demanded **rises** (inverse relation) → the demand curve slopes **downward**.
**Movement along** (change in quantity demanded, due to own price) vs **shift** (change in demand, due to income, tastes, related goods).
**Normal goods** (demand rises with income) vs **inferior goods** (demand falls with income); **substitutes and complements**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Law of Diminishing Marginal Utility: MU falls with more consumption.
Consumer equilibrium (one good): MU = price; (two goods): MUx/Px = MUy/Py.
Indifference curve = equal satisfaction; convex (diminishing MRS); higher = better.
Consumer equilibrium (ordinal): budget line tangent to highest indifference curve.
Law of Demand: price ↓ → quantity demanded ↑ (downward-sloping curve).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Marginal utility diminishes** as more is consumed (Law of DMU).
**Consumer equilibrium: MU per rupee equal across goods (MUx/Px = MUy/Py)**.
**Indifference curves are convex and never intersect**.
**Movement along** = quantity demanded (own price); **shift** = demand (income/tastes/related goods).
